'''Sapphire''' was a [[Gender/Legends|female]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] born circa [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] whose [[Parent/Legends|parents]] [[Death/Legends|died]] in an accident due to an error made by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Officer/Legends|officer]] [[Dane Tizzin]]. Following their deaths, Sapphire became a smuggler and helped the [[Scoundrel/Legends|scoundrel]] [[Kevas Startron]] in his last run. As a reward for her assistance during the run, he gave her his [[Starship/Legends|ship]], a [[Hyrotii Corporation/Legends|Hyrotil]] [[Crescent-class Transport|''Crescent''-class transport]] that she named ''[[Sapphire's Gem]]''. Becoming the [[Captain/Legends|captain]] and only crew member of the ''Gem'', she customized the ship with new technology to make it stealthier and faster. Although young, she became an outlaw because of her smuggling activities in several [[Star system/Legends|systems]].

Sapphire was secretly a [[Courier/Legends|courier]] for the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] and a contact of [[General/Legends|General]] [[Airen Cracken/Legends|Airen Cracken]]. She also spent time searching for Tizzin, in hopes of getting revenge on him for the death of her parents.

==Biography==
Born in approximately [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]]<ref name="Birth" /> to two maintenance [[Technician/Legends|technicians]] who specialized in [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE fighters]], Sapphire spent her childhood in several [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] bases because her parents were forced to travel due to their work. When Sapphire was a teenager, she sought to join the [[Imperial Academy/Legends|Imperial Academy]]. However, her parents were [[Death/Legends|killed]] in an explosion caused by a blunder made by [[Dane Tizzin]], a young Imperial [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenant]]. As Tizzin's family was well-connected, he was not accused; instead, Sapphire's parents were blamed. From that moment on, Sapphire wanted to exact vengeance on Tizzin.<ref name="cro" />

Unable to join the Academy, Sapphire turned to [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggling]] for a living. She happened to be friends with [[Kevas Startron]], an old smuggler and owner of the [[Hyrotii Corporation/Legends|Hyrotil]] [[Crescent-class Transport|''Crescent'' transport]] [[Sapphire's Gem|''New Cov Quasar'']]. Startron was planning to retire after one last smuggling run, and he asked Sapphire to be his partner. With Startron's health declining, Sapphire was forced to do most of the job. Upon conclusion of the run, Sapphire lied about her involvement so that Startron would get the credit for it. Grateful for her support, the [[Scoundrel/Legends|scoundrel]] gave his [[Starship/Legends|ship]] to Sapphire, who renamed it ''Sapphire's Gem'' and made several customizations to it&mdash;she modified the ship to make it both fast and furtive, adding [[Sensor/Legends|sensor]]-disrupting technology such as special [[Deflector shield/Legends|shields]] that hid power emanations to avoid detection. She also replaced the energy weapons with fire-linked [[Concussion missile/Legends|concussion missile]] systems that, while less aggressive, were easier to hide from enemy sensors. As the ship required a crew of only one, Sapphire [[Pilot/Legends|piloted]] it alone as its [[Captain/Legends|captain]]. Soon, she became a fugitive in several [[Star system/Legends|systems]] on charges of smuggling, bribery, and avoiding arrest.<ref name="cro" />

At the beginning of her smuggling career, Sapphire was looking for the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]], a clandestine rebel movement that opposed the Empire. She later joined the Alliance and secretly became a [[Courier/Legends|courier]] for the group, pretending to be uninvolved in [[Politics/Legends|politics]] in order to hide her affiliation. Sapphire worked alongside Alliance [[General/Legends|General]] [[Airen Cracken/Legends|Airen Cracken]], setting up raids on Imperial convoys. For a long time, Sapphire searched for Tizzin, but was unable to find him.<ref name="cro" /> Years later, her connection to the Rebel Alliance was a not-so-well-kept secret. At that time, Tizzin had became a [[Commodore/Legends|commodore]] and [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Naval]] attaché to the staff of the [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] of the [[Kira sector/Legends|Kira sector]]. When an [[Assassin/Legends|assassination]] attempt was made against the Commodore, a young Imperial officer by the name of [[Lynx Reglis]] impersonated Sapphire to save Tizzin's life.<ref name="ss">''[[Stock Ships]]''</ref>

==Personality and traits==
Around [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]], at twenty-two years of age, Sapphire was an efficient smuggler who used her knowledge about Imperial [[Navy/Legends|naval]] procedures to her benefit. Her bright [[Color/Legends|green]] [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] and short red hair attracted the attention of people first meeting her; many of them considered Sapphire a beautiful woman. Although young, she earned General Airen Cracken's respect and admiration. Years after her parents' death, Sapphire still remembered Dane Tizzin's involvement in their deaths and planned to exact vengeance.<ref name="cro" />

Sapphire dressed in a one-piece black body suit with blue highlights, not discarding other complements such as belts and vests. She used both a [[Heavy blaster pistol/Legends|heavy blaster pistol]] and a [[Vibrosword/Legends|vibrosword]]. She also carried a [[Datapad/Legends|datapad]], a [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]], and three [[Medpac/Legends|medpacs]] with her.<ref name="cro" />

==Behind the scenes==
Sapphire was first mentioned in ''[[Cracken's Rebel Operatives]]'' ([[1994]]), a supplement to ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'' that was published by [[West End Games]], edited by [[Bill Smith]], and written by several authors. [[Dan Verssen]] is credited as the designer of the section mentioning Sapphire. The book included an image of Sapphire drawn by [[Doug Shuler]]. In [[1997]], Sapphire was mentioned in another [[Roleplaying game|roleplaying]] book, ''[[Stock Ships]]'', which was edited by [[Paul Sudlow]] and [[Eric S. Trautmann]].
